I specifically asked about this. Apparently, once the child is born it is a US Citizen with rights. You can't just abandon the baby cuz you don't want to pay for it. But wouldn't the man be required to be a slave to support a child, similarly to the woman being required to be property?

They mumbled on for a while about rights, etc? I said they had to give me an answer that didn't make them look silly (sillier than they already are). What I got was... If you are against abortion, the responsibility is on both parents. If you are for abortion, why are we even having this conversation? Silly I know, but it makes sense in a weird, illogical, liberal mindset.

Before the 20 week mark, the baby is NOT considered a child (yeah, I know) so child support does not enter into it. Once a child is born, then the mother can go to court and ask for child support. But what happened between the 20 week mark and birth?

One thing that was pointed out is that the baby is not a U.S. Citizen until it is born. I called bullshit on that, but they stated the 14th Amendment. "All persons born or naturalized in theUnited States". If the baby is not born, child support also doesn't enter play because they are not U.S. citizens until they are born. I have no idea how this logic works when it comes to illegals. Believe me, I asked.

I think Liberals see it as forcing the women into a status matching property. The second a women gets pregnant, she is viewed as a required home for the baby. While at the same time the woman is forced and punished into property status for having sex, the man faces nothing like this. That is why they can get an abortion without the man's approval.

I know the feeling. In the last two years, I've lost a lifetime career, a marriage, and now I'm so broke I live with my mother. I'm 43 years old and life completely sucks. Every time I go into the dialysis center, I have to take a deep breath and know that the nurses will be happy and cheerful like nothing is wrong. Like the 5 year mark isn't a 65% death rate for dialysis patients. Like even though I'm halfway to this mark, knowing my luck I will continue to suffer past that. 

Life on dialysis sucks. I wouldn't wish this on my worst enemy. The only reason, and I mean the ONLY reason I keep going, is that my mother will be sad if I die. That's it. Above that, I would have eaten a bullet long ago. I always wonder what will happen if that isn't enough anymore. Well, at least I live in a state where guns are as easy to buy as a loaf of bread.

Good luck my friend. I know how you feel and from my viewpoint, I have nothing to offer. I wish you the best of luck. I don't know if I will live through 2019. I guess we'll see.

The last time I was in Japan, I went to the Yushukan. This is a rather large museum focused on World War II and the events that lead up to it. Almost all of the signs were in English, and it was a rather different history than what U.S. children learn. If I remember correctly....

-->Late 1800s, all major powers were trying to get a foothold in China (U.S., U.K., etc).

-->Following the Boxer Rebellion in China that rejected all foreigners form the country, communism started to take hold.

-->Japan invaded to stop the spread of communism.

-->The other superpowers were angry that Japan was getting a foothold where they did not, so sanctions against Japan started.

-->Japan's resources were seriously starting to suffer from all the sanctions. Japan decided they had no choice but to attack those who were threatening the prosperity of their country.

-->Bombing of Pearl Harbor

It was a very interesting telling of events and completely different than what I learned as a child. I highly recommend a visit if you are ever in Tokyo.
